notes:
Top-line: Mid-market SaaS (support agent product) migrating from incumbent due to recurring latency regressions on streaming endpoints.

Current situation:
- Using incumbent API for chat + tool-calls; last quarter saw multiple user complaints about slow streaming and truncated tool responses.
- Team expects sub-300ms token latency for conversational UX; peak concurrency ~150-200 concurrent users during PST peak.
- Primary aim: validate Redwood hosted streaming can meet SLO and maintain cost parity; if successful, evaluate Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput.

POC scope (agreed verbally):
- 2-week perf run: compare Redwood hosted streaming vs incumbent on identical workload (same prompts, tool-calling chains).
- Metrics: end-to-end streaming latency (median, p95), token-cost, failure/retry rate, tool-call latency.
- Dataset: 2k representative conversations (support flows), simulated concurrency up to 200 users.
- Integration: webhook tool-calling demo + function call tracing; include KV prefix cache scenario.

Stakeholders: Jordan Kim (AE, owner), Priya Patel (SE), Marco Ruiz (Eng lead - DialogueCraft), Head of Product: Laila Fernandez.

Key quotes / signals:
- "If Redwood can demonstrably beat our current provider on streaming latency AND not blow up costs, we'll move the traffic." — Marco Ruiz
- Pricing sensitivity: appetite for 3-mo dedicated pilot to prove economics before annual commit.

Open items / risks:
- Incumbent has a renewal window in 30 days — need fast POC + pricing to influence decision.
- Security: need SOC2 report and confirmation around audit logs and KMS integration.
- Data residency: some EU customers require region pinning; DialogueCraft expects Redwood to document residency options.
